This game has everything you need for a great game, but then it falls short. Literaly its SHORT. SUPER SHORT. When you think the story get's rolling, the only thing that gets rolling are the credits. I have never been that dissapointed in a game, and I played mass effect 3 with it's amateur ending.
The only thing I can say 

DO NOT BUY!!!

Take you money and go watch a movie or buy yourself a book, even with a bad one at least you get a proper ending.
This game wasted so much potential. It's like the devs had the beginning of a great story, started to program the game before they had the story completed. And after chapter one they ran out of steam but published the game with a makeshift ending. 

AGAIN DO NOT BUY!!

I Recommend this game, almost everything about the game was great. The twists, The mystery, the gameplay, and the story. I hope the devs can follow in their own footsteps and learn from this. 

However i felt the game to be too short, I think 2 or 3 more days should have been added sort of like filler or sort of time jumps/skips, everything you do happens within the span of 3-4 days its kinda just weird. What I mean is it would have helped with the world building if not every case was connected and certain game play mechanics were used way more. For example they run you down how to use a chemical scanner that you only use once. there is a car database that you never technically use beyond scanning one number plate. These mechanics served to build the world up but didn't make for very engaging gameplay. 

Actually the game would have benefitted if it didn't dive right into the deep end at the beginning and gradually dove in.

Lets just say I wish it was more papers please or beholder then what I actuially got, I was hoping for more cases, less grounding, more case of the week/monster of the week type of game. doesn't lessen the game, that was just my expectation for the game.

The only downside of the game is the ending, [spoiler]Everything you did up until the ending felt absolutely useless as you die, everyone around you dies and the mysterious organisation stays mysterious. for me I can't stand these types of endings, I like closure, its like how RDR2 and RDR1 work despite the protagonist dying, there is closure. Here I don't get that and it somewhat spoils the game for me because it makes me feel like i wasted time. It's like if Harry Potter dies in Book 3, and the last 4 Books are about Neville. What's the point of introducing all these characters and not giving any of them closure. The worst part about it, the ending comes after a massive twist to your identity, a twist that gets immediately ruined by the death of you.[spoiler] even after all that i still reccomend the game wholeheartedly because the story and twist was amazing.

My jaw dropped multiple times, and I found myself wondering if I was solving the puzzle, or just a piece of the puzzle in someones plan. Anyways, great game, best played in one 3-4 hour session. After this game, I think its possible to have PTSD from a video game

I was *soooo* sucked into *The Operator*! What an incredible little gem of a game. It’s a short, narrative-driven adventure that doesn’t try to wow you with complex mechanics—and honestly, it doesn’t need to. The gameplay is just a backdrop for a gripping, well-staged story that makes fantastic use of the video game medium.  

The way the story unfolds is just *chef’s kiss*—exciting, immersive, and full of tension. I especially loved the “cutscenes.” Even though they probably used very few resources, they built a *ton* of atmosphere. Seriously clever stuff.  

It’s not flashy, but it’s smart and stylish in all the right ways. If you’re into interactive stories and atmospheric thrillers, this is such a satisfying experience. My only complaint? I want *more*.  

Please, devs—give us more games like this!
It left me wishing the story was more believable and cohesive, though it was a great buildup to the end.

By the end, I felt like I had just taken part in one of the best thriller films I've seen in a long, long time. If you're a fan of Crime Thrillers, this game has your name all over it.

I had fun. I also almost requested a refund after finishing it because the ending made me so angry. [spoiler]It's not a happy ending, which is fine, but it's also not a satisfying ending. Choices are ultimately meaningless because an apparently superhuman hitman escapes custody in a high-security building (the story even makes a point of saying how secure this building is when you're helping another character find the passkey for the locker room) and is then apparently omniscient as he knows exactly where to find the director of this highly secure organization during a security lockdown, exactly when to intercept to main character en route to the exit, and is then able to ascend from the parking garage to the eighth floor to eliminate the supervisor/insider contact of our benevolent hacker companion all apparently without facing the slightest resistance from security in what is basically this universe's FBI HQ. Did the mole have him memorize the layout of the entire building? For what reason? After all that you're treated to a series of newspaper headlines letting you know that absolutely every ally you had over the course of the game is either dead, imprisoned, or missing. All tension goes out the window and it just turns into a cascade of tragedy for no clear reason. It's just so unbelievable to me. Maybe if it was clear from the start that this was more like a part 1 to a larger story or something, I would be more forgiving, but I expected a satisfying conclusion when I bought the game. Not super-hitman destroys everything because *dismissive raspberry sounds*[/spoiler]

With all that said, I do think the developer has a lot of potential. The puzzles were interesting and solving them felt really satisfying.
Plot twists and some surprises near the end were predictable but a great experience nonetheless

I really like the genre of mystery games but The Operator felt like it fell short in a few categories for me to recommend this as is. I think they tried to do some interesting things, but I found the story to be a little too 'on rails' for me, and a little too short for the price point. 

One way I'd describe TO is to imagine the intro to a story where you're shown a vast map of the world with a story about it's history and maybe even a quick introduction to the strange artifact you'll be using to navigate the world... And then to only interact with 3% of the map, and to gloss over the history, and the artifact is just a paperweight that we'll never use more than once. That's fine but it does feel like someone went through a lot of trouble to flesh out this world only for it to shrink down to a tiny slice of what they'd made. 

Personally, I'm also not a huge fan of the story. I think they tried to go in a series of different directions at the same time (are you going to play it by the straight and narrow? Are you going to go rogue?) and it all led to the same one place so none of your choices really mattered. The big reveal hinges on you believing that the game's limitations are intentional and not a contrivance of some grand design, so the payout for their big reveals never really felt as good as they could've been. 

So... yeah? I think the story's a little weak/ watered down, but it lives in a frame that I could see the developer building into a bigger/ broader story that would be fun to play. The bones are here for something that could be a cool mystery game, but I'd sooner recommend 'The Roottrees are dead' if you're looking for a better/ more rewarding mystery to sink your time into.

I wanted to like this game, and for the four hours I played, it was enjoyable, but not great. 

Pros:
* Creative mechanics are employed here, it has good promise
* There were some good AHA! moments that were fun
* This is a personal one, but I always appreciate when developers make it playable on my Mac Air

Cons:
* This is really more an interactive novel with some puzzle elements than a game. In addition to its short play time, your choices have little to no impact, it really doesn't matter what you choose in many conversations. 
* There's a lot of moments between the actual gameplay bits that feel like time padding, like I would have skipped if given the chance. 
* The writing is just ok, nothing special. The characters could be fleshed out a bit more, I think
* Without spoiling anything, the ending is pretty unsatisfying imo.

Overall, just an ok game, but could be great. I hope the developers continue to grow.

Not a masterpiece, but definitely worth a shot, get on sale and get three hours well spent.

I absolutely loved the mechanics and story line of this game. I had a great time playing, and I certainly would have played much more if the game was longer and less linear. I finished the game in a couple days, and even for a linear game it felt a little shorter than I wanted. I feel like there should have been more cases that weren't related to the main plot. I think the game could have benefited from a few more hours of content, especially just basic operator tasks that don't progress the main plot. More opportunities to be challenged like disarming the bomb, which was extremely fun. I also feel this game could have had multiple endings depending on how you play. I only say this because I would have kept playing if I didn't run out of content. The tools and puzzles of this game have so much potential and you could have a huge variety of cases to solve or emergencies to handle. I'll be following for more in the future, so I hope you make more games like this! Thank you for such an entertaining game!
